reading_mnemonic: Now you can use that box to store all your hardcore (はこ) punk vinyl records. You're a real connoisseur, so you know that hardcore music should only ever be kept in bamboo boxes.

meaning_mnemonic: The rice radical and rice kanji are the same in looks and meaning. This kanji can also mean America, maybe because America is covered in rice or fields or something?
reading_mnemonic: A ton of rice is grown in America. And yet you never see rice in American cuisine. So where's all that unused rice going? Actually, it all gets dumped into a big bay (べい). They have too much rice and no place to store it, so they've started using bays to store it.

meaning_mnemonic: You tie a thread on your finger before jumping in the pool to remind yourself of the promise you made to your mother. The thread represents the promise you made to mow the lawn after you finished swimming in the pool.
reading_mnemonic: After you get out of the pool, you keep the promise you made to your mother. So you get on your yak (やく) powered mower and trim the grass. Yes, your mower is pulled by a yak. It’s very efficient.

meaning_mnemonic: Sew thread through your top hat and to the top hats of other people you know and you'll turn into a group of top hat wearing people. You're all connected by the thread now, so everyone will assume you're a group, even if that's all you guys have going for yourselves.
reading_mnemonic: Everyone in this group loves cumin (くみ). You know, the spice or seed. The group take off their top hats and fill them with cumin. You're officially a group for lovers of cumin.

meaning_mnemonic: Tying a thread to a tombstone each year will help you manage the passage of time. That way you’ll know how many years you pass through, since you’ll have one thread for each year to count.
reading_mnemonic: Dealing with the passage of time can be tough, so after you tie the thread to the tombstone, each year you eat a piece of cake (けい). You already eat cake to mark the passage of time on your birthday, so why not here as well?

meaning_mnemonic: When a bunch of threads are meeting on paper (after you've dipped them in paint, say) they can create a masterpiece of a picture (or painting).
reading_mnemonic: You tell someone you painted this masterpiece of a picture. Their response? "EH (え)?!"

meaning_mnemonic: You have to gather thread to sell if you want to continue living. You want to make a living, don't you? Make sure you continue to sell that thread every single day!
reading_mnemonic: You have to continue to sell that thread because a Bosozoku (ぞく) bike gang is forcing you to do it. You see? If you want to continue to live, you have to appease this Bosozoku gang. You better keep selling!

meaning_mnemonic: Put a net around a criminal to show their guilt. Criminals look like anyone else on the street, so you decide to tie them in nets to make sure people know who they're dealing with.
reading_mnemonic: The guilt shows on the criminal's face. They smile, shrug, and pull a stolen xylophone (ざい) out of their back pocket.

meaning_mnemonic: A sheep that's big is a true beauty. Big is beautiful, and that's all the more true for sheep.
reading_mnemonic: The big sheep's beauty has attracted a swarm of bees (び). The sheep is so beautiful that the bees have mistaken it for a flower.

meaning_mnemonic: By the time you finish digging a coffin hole with nothing but a spoon, you’ll be an old elderly person. Digging with nothing but a spoon takes a long time, especially when the hole needs to be big enough for a coffin. You might as well be digging it for yourself at this rate. By the time you finish, you’ll be all wrinkled and elderly and just about ready to keel over.
reading_mnemonic: Now that you’re elderly (and probably about to die) you suddenly crave some delicious roe (ろう). Salmon roe, sea urchin roe, tofugu roe, doesn’t matter. Your old, tired bones need roe after all that hard work!

meaning_mnemonic: The ear radical and ear kanji are the same in looks as well as meaning.
reading_mnemonic: Put your hand to your ear and sing... "Mimimimimimiiiii!" (みみ) and listen to your tone with your ear.

meaning_mnemonic: Give trash to the moon and it will nurture and raise that trash like it's its own little moon baby.
reading_mnemonic: The moon nurtures the trash ball until one day, it speaks! "行く (いく), 行く！" it says. It wants to go live with mom moon!

meaning_mnemonic: In a private place on the moon, you hide two spoons that give you a special ability. It's the ability to predict the future! The private moon spoons reflect the knowledge of time and space into your brain. Now that's a cool ability!
reading_mnemonic: This ability to predict the future makes you famous and now everyone knows your name: Nostradamus (のう)! And now that people know about your name and special ability, everyone will love you!

meaning_mnemonic: Your boat has fins and a mouth! It's still a boat though.
reading_mnemonic: This boat belongs to the centaurs (せん). That's probably why you've never seen a boat like it before.

meaning_mnemonic: A drop of water to a root is good. It's good for the roots to grow and live and thrive. And what's good for roots is good for our plants and us humans too.
reading_mnemonic: A good way to get a lot of drops of water for your roots is to buy a row boat (りょう). Then just row out to the middle of the lake and plonk all the roots right into the source!

meaning_mnemonic: There are flowers on your right to show that you're still young. Your body still works, you're happy, you have your entire life ahead of you! And everything smells like flowers.
reading_mnemonic: When young people look to the right, they'll see their future: a walker (わか). You know, those metal contraptions with tennis balls on the bottoms to make sure they don't scrape the floor. Everything may be flowers and happiness now, but your future is in a walker.

meaning_mnemonic: The flowers have grown old, so they're suffering.
reading_mnemonic: If a flower or a person is growing old and suffering, give them a cookie (く).

meaning_mnemonic: You plant your flowers in the light of the sun in the shape of a cross, but it's too hot—the sun is too strong—and you end up with grass. Flowers can't grow in these conditions.
reading_mnemonic: The grass on top is brown and burned from the sun, so you need to take a cool saw (くさ) and hack the tops off. The saw is actually physically cool to the touch, to help heal the grass' sunburned bits. It just happens to look cool too.

meaning_mnemonic: Flowers are knocked down by a violent tsunami, and swirl through the air to kiss your face gently as they fall. With the tsunami came a great windy storm that blew the flowers down. Amongst all the destruction, it's a pretty sight to watch them fall.
reading_mnemonic: You want to save these flowers that fall around you, so you take out a drying rack (らく) and place them carefully on it. Any flowers that fall will go on the rack like this, so can save them for later.

meaning_mnemonic: Flowers bring beauty to the world of trees, but the leaf is what matters the most. Leaves are how flowers and trees get their nutrients from the sun!
reading_mnemonic: Picture a little flower working really hard to grow its first leaf. The leaf pops out and it shouts, "Ha (は)!"

meaning_mnemonic: Flowers can be used for comfort, but also for medicine. Sure, it’s a comfort to smell flowers because they smell nice, but one can also use them as medicine to heal people.
reading_mnemonic: The best way to transport all the medicine on land is with a yak (やく). Yaks are big, strong, and very capable of transporting flower medicine like these.

meaning_mnemonic: There go some angels with drops on their shoulders. Carrying drops like that requires technique. It’s a real art.
reading_mnemonic: Angels are so good at this because they are trained in ninjutsu (じゅつ), or the "ninja techniques." Everyone knows that ninjas are great at carrying drops on the go!

meaning_mnemonic: Sometimes life gives you a kick, and you have to express yourself to deal with it! How do you express yourself? On the surface (of your face)!
reading_mnemonic: You need to express yourself, so you call up a friend and say "Heyo!" (ひょう).

meaning_mnemonic: When a helicopter is piloted by a woman, it stirs an insatiable need in her. She doesn't know what it is. But she needs it. And that's why she's flying around looking for it!
reading_mnemonic: Finally she knows what she needs! It's yogurt (よう)! Delicious, creamy yogurt!

meaning_mnemonic: Viking see, Viking memorize. That’s how Vikings learn things. They see something, and then they memorize it. Quite simple, really. It can also mean awake. Just remember that Vikings can't see if they aren't awake. There won't be anything to memorize if their eyes are still closed, after all!
reading_mnemonic: Every morning, a cock (かく) crows and rouses the Vikings. Seeing this, one of the Vikings memorizes the cock crow so that he can mimic it and play pranks on his fellow Vikings.

meaning_mnemonic: Angle your sword correctly at this cow to solve its riddle. The key is to untie the cow with the sword without hurting it.
reading_mnemonic: Did I mention that you have to solve this whole riddle while on a kayak (かい)? No?! Whoops.

meaning_mnemonic: What you say to oneself (yourself), you decide to write down. Whether this is in the form of a journal, diary, or blog, you feel the need to record these important thoughts in some way.
reading_mnemonic: You need to protect what you write down and record for yourself with a key (き). These are your special thoughts and feelings, you don't want anyone else to see! Lock them away with a key!

meaning_mnemonic: Say it at noon. That's the only time I will allow you to say it. That's the only time I will permit you to say it. Other than that, no saying anything. Noon is your window.
reading_mnemonic: Where do these archaic horrible rules exist? The smaller version of Kyoto, Little Kyoto (きょ). Normal Kyoto is just fine. This smaller one is where a group of people went to create their own little town with their own dumb rules.

meaning_mnemonic: Whatever people say to you will be carved by a blade into your heart. Sounds cruel, but it's a way to make you recognize their power.
reading_mnemonic: Having their words carved into your heart makes you recognize the authority of many people. But the only one you could ever truly acknowledge, is Nintendo (にん).

meaning_mnemonic: What do you say to a guard? Your theory about how the thing he's guarding isn't even real. Yeah, you have this whole thing figured out. You have for a while. At this point, it's only fair that you tell your theory to the guard who's wasting his time.
reading_mnemonic: The guard listens to your theory but then he says his OWN! He thinks there are two sets (せつ) of guarded items, and he's only guarding one. According to his theory, either one could be real! His theory is more plausible, don't you think?

meaning_mnemonic: You say something about the circumference of this area. You've looked around this whole area, making a big circle around it, because you are trying to investigate something that happened here. You also say this thing in a really quiet tone of voice, because you don't want the person or thing you're investigating to know you're on to them.
reading_mnemonic: "I came here to investigate this place, and I did indeed find out who the criminal is... it's none other than Mrs. Chou (ちょう)!"

meaning_mnemonic: You say things around a fire. In fact there are two fires, and you're talking with a group of people, all sitting around two nice campfires.
reading_mnemonic: You talk in this intense, fiery way all the way until dawn (だん), but no longer! Once dawn comes the discussion needs to be concluded.

meaning_mnemonic: You say, throwing your hat on the ground in front of the bookshelf, "I have a theory!" All this reading and thinking has finally given you a wonderful idea, a theory you think might solve all of your problems!
reading_mnemonic: "What is your theory, Ron (ろん)?" asks Hermione. You're Ron Weasley, and you just came up with a theory that you think will help you stop Voldemort.

meaning_mnemonic: If you can say what sound a drunkard makes, you must be very discerning. Few people are able to discern what sound a drunkard makes, but you — you can say, because you're a very discriminating listener.
reading_mnemonic: Discerning individuals like you are considered chic (しき). What's more chic than your discriminating way of listening?

meaning_mnemonic: You have a poem about winter that you say to warn people against going outside. It's cold and dangerous in winter! You admonish anyone and everyone you see going out there with your scary winter poem.
reading_mnemonic: To make sure people listen to your warning, you threaten to take away their cake (けい). People will do anything for cake, so when you bring it up, they actually take your attempts to warn them about winter seriously.

meaning_mnemonic: What you say is righteousness, at least that's what you believe. You keep talking and saying these things, and you don't listen to anyone else's words. This is your style of deliberation and discussion.
reading_mnemonic: What are you in deliberation about? Whether or not to send some poor soul to the guillotine (ぎ). "I think he should go," you say. "I don't think he should," says another. This deliberation is going nowhere...

meaning_mnemonic: When you're in prison, whoever ends up with the shellfish will lose. It's the game all prisoners play. It's like keep away from the shellfish. And if you end up with the shellfish BZZZZTT that's it, you're the loser.
reading_mnemonic: If you lose, you're a fool (ふ). All you had to do was not hold the prison shellfish. It really shouldn't have been that hard to not lose, ya fool.

meaning_mnemonic: Give some shellfish to a talented person and they'll have no problem accumulating wealth. People with talent can make money out of pretty much anything, so shellfish are like easy-mode.
reading_mnemonic: This talented person really starts accumulating wealth when their cyborg (さい) is unveiled. It's a half-man, half-shellfish cyborg that plays the xylophone (ざい), and everyone wants to buy it.

meaning_mnemonic: The life of a shellfish is filled with blame. They take the blame for everything from food poisoning and allergies, to cutting people's feet on beaches.
reading_mnemonic: When those poor shellfish aren't having blame piled on them, they're being eaten, because shellfish are thought to make for a very sexy (せき) meal.

meaning_mnemonic: The next shellfish will be yours, but this shellfish will be mine. These are the resources we have to share and distribute.
reading_mnemonic: You save up all of your resources so you can buy a sheep (し). You bring a big sack of your shellfish resources to the market and finally get to pick out that sheep you've had your eyes on for months.

meaning_mnemonic: If you've been walking all day, your foot is the last thing anyone would want to kiss, especially after wandering barefoot down a road. Your feet are filthy, sweaty, and stinky. Nobody is going to want to kiss those feet.
reading_mnemonic: What was this person walking down again? Oh, that's right – a road (ろ). They were walking down a filthy road.

meaning_mnemonic: When your tongue becomes too spicy for you to bear, it’s time to quit the jalapeño eating contest. You’ve been eating them for three hours now and the spiciness from the peppers is really burning your tongue. Throw in the towel, it’s time to quit the contest. This kanji has another meaning too: Eating isn't the only thing that makes your tongue spicy, so do certain words. Say your favorite words out loud right now. Feel them on your tongue. Words are the spicy food of language!
reading_mnemonic: Oh, you're probably wondering who won that spicy food contest after you quit and became obsessed with words instead. It was Jesus (じ). Who did you expect? He was great with words AND never quitting when things got spicy.

meaning_mnemonic: Your scooter is anti scoot. It doesn't want to run. So you have to return it.
reading_mnemonic: You return to the store and wait in line to return the scooter but the person working returns doesn't want you to return it. He stares you dead in the eyes, waves his hand, and turns you into a hen (へん)!

meaning_mnemonic: On a scooter there is a bear with a drop on its head trying to follow and chase you! You accidentally splashed it with water and it's not happy about it. You're on your own scooter, luckily, but that doesn't make this any less terrifying.
reading_mnemonic: The bear is trying to follow you because it wants your obi (お) as compensation for its injured pride. The obi is waving in the wind behind your scooter, and the bear is reaching out with its teeth to try and grab it.

meaning_mnemonic: You jump on your scooter with a big bundle to go as fast as you can! You have a bundle of pizzas in here, and they need to be delivered as fast as you can get them there!
reading_mnemonic: You were going so fast, you only put on socks (そく). So now you're barreling down the street at top speeds in just your sad, white socks.

meaning_mnemonic: Your scooter and your car is what you always take along with you. Make sure they're connected well so you don't lose them!
reading_mnemonic: You take along your scooter and your car. Anything else, you can do a rental (れん) for!

meaning_mnemonic: You give your scooter to a turkey so that it can advance. The turkey was trying and failing to walk through a crowded street, so out of the goodness of your heart you gave it a scooter so it could advance.
reading_mnemonic: You wave as the turkey advances into the street at top speeds, collides with a car, and scrapes up its shins (しん) almost immediately. Ah!

meaning_mnemonic: While riding on your scooter, you grow a mustache on top of the mustache you already have in order to surpass the people around you. You're in a scooter race and your mustache is the only thing keeping you in the lead, but someone else has a mustache too! So you grow another mustache to surpass them once again!
reading_mnemonic: Suddenly, something else manages to surpass you all. It's a car (か)! A car with two mustaches is also riding on a scooter and going way faster than you.

meaning_mnemonic: You ride your scooter through the dirt while carrying a sheep because you're determined to attain something. Greatness? Glory? Everlasting fame? Maybe you'll attain a plural combination of all those things. After all, you are the best sheep-carrying off-road scooterist the world has ever seen.
reading_mnemonic: After you attain that plural combination of glory, greatness, and fame, you get a tattoo (たつ) to celebrate: "world's greatest," in gothic lettering, above a picture of you and your sheep on your scooter.

meaning_mnemonic: You see a scooter with a zombie on it, going really far away. Someone tied that zombie to the scooter and now it's far off in the distance, groaning and growling.
reading_mnemonic: The zombie goes so far, that its life ends (えん). Zombies need to eat to live (it's really all they need), but they go so far on their scooter trip, that they just give up and end it all.

meaning_mnemonic: You want to get a scooter, so you have one self (oneself) and another self working together to choose. The two tiny yous sit on each of your shoulders, like angel and devil, and argue about which scooter you should choose.
reading_mnemonic: Suddenly your selfs both gasp and choose a scooter in front of you that looks like a centaur (せん). The scooter is designed like a human on the top, the bars are its arms, and the bottom with the seat and the wheels are all horse. This centaur scooter is what you choose to ride.

meaning_mnemonic: Someones and buildings, someones and buildings, someones and buildings. So many someones and buildings. With so many someones and buildings, we have ourselves a metropolis.
reading_mnemonic: In this metropolis everything is a toe (と). The someones are toes, walking around. The buildings are toes, too.

meaning_mnemonic: You don't want to keep all the alcohol to yourself (oneself), so you distribute it to all of your friends. Heck, not just your friends, to everyone you can find!
reading_mnemonic: As you distribute the alcohol you say a haiku (はい): Here you go my friends Alcohol for everyone Never drink alone

meaning_mnemonic: A tsunami is an alcoholic beverage containing a lot of alcohol. It’s 3 different kinds of rums, pineapple juice, and grenadine. It’ll hit you like a tsunami though. This alcoholic drink has a kick to it.
reading_mnemonic: As you lie on this beach, the alcohol keeps coming down a chute (しゅ), straight into your mouth. You can feel the sand in your toes and the alcohol sliding down your throat from this special tsunami chute.

meaning_mnemonic: This gate of horns will take you to heaven. These horns are related and connected to heaven in some way.
reading_mnemonic: They are related and connected to heaven because these are the horns that Genghis Khan (かん) made from his enemies. God said he could come into heaven if he made a gate of horns, so that's what he did.

meaning_mnemonic: Going into a building made by a squid is risky. First of all, squids only have tentacles, no bones, and they make all of their buildings out of risky materials like kelp and sharp coral.
reading_mnemonic: "It's too risky, leave me!" the squid cries. "I'll save you, underwater citizen! Nothing is too risky for Ken (けん) the samurai!" The building is collapsing on the squid, the risk is so great, but Ken the samurai dives in and saves him!

meaning_mnemonic: This building has easy access to sunshine. The sunlight shines right in, because it's a clear building.
reading_mnemonic: The sunshine gets into the building so easily, in fact, that it hits your yogurt (よう). The sunshine makes the yogurt... gross.

meaning_mnemonic: Buildings hold festivals on special occasions.
reading_mnemonic: The occasion this time is to celebrate your wonderful cyborg (さい). It's about time you did something nice for it.

meaning_mnemonic: A Chinese turkey is difficult to find because they are so rare. Chinese turkeys are the rarest variety of turkey, so naturally, finding one is exceedingly difficult.
reading_mnemonic: Do you know the actual reason Chinese turkey are so difficult to find? It’s because they’re all made out of Naan (なん). Of course they’re elusive when they blend in so well with all the other Naan!

meaning_mnemonic: When rain falls on Wolverine, it turns to snow. He's so emotionally distant and cold that the rain freezes into snow as soon as it gets near him.
reading_mnemonic: You're concerned for Wolverine's mental health. Him being so emotionally cold that he turns rain to snow means you keep (ゆき) asking if he's okay. But that only makes him want to be more distant.

meaning_mnemonic: Within the blue water, a conflict stirs, but is made quiet by the muffling power of liquid. Under this blue water is a great conflict between two sea monsters, but on the surface it appears peaceful and quiet as the water prevents sound from rising above the surface.
reading_mnemonic: As you watch below the quiet water, every once in a while a saber (せい) breaches the surface and quietly slices back down.

meaning_mnemonic: A criminal has done an injustice on the world or other people. Being a criminal is a negative thing, and even if it was just a mistake, it was still a crime.
reading_mnemonic: When you commit an injustice, you'll know because heat (ひ) fills your body. Maybe you've never done any kind of big thing, but when you make a mistake your face fills with heat and you turn red!

meaning_mnemonic: The face radical and the face kanji are the same! But this isn't just a face like the one you're looking at your computer/phone with. It's the surface kind of face too!
reading_mnemonic: This face you're looking at, that has a lot of surface area, belongs to men (めん). Not a single man, but all men put together. It's hundreds of thousands of men's faces in a row.

meaning_mnemonic: If you feed a lot of beans to a geoduck, its head will grow larger. To a geoduck, beans are a brain food, so by eating beans, it can grow an incredibly large head. Geoducks already look strange enough as it is, let alone with engorged heads.
reading_mnemonic: As the geoduck eats more and more beans its head gets bigger and bigger, until finally the head explodes like an atomic (あたま) bomb. BOOM! Geoduck parts go flying everywhere and pieces of its massive head float to the ground as atomic fallout.

meaning_mnemonic: You stand on a cliff, a hair's breadth away from the edge, when out of nowhere a geoduck slaps you in the face. The force makes you back away from the edge of the cliff, and your face is all slimy from the geoduck's residue.
reading_mnemonic: But where did that geoduck come from? As you turn from the cliff edge, you find yourself face-to-face with a cow (かお). This cow is the one who hit you in the face with a geoduck. You don't know why, but something about your face has upset the cow.
radical_breakdown: 立|Stand, 厂|Cliff, 彡|Hair, 頁|Geoduck

meaning_mnemonic: The original geoduck had a request. He wants there to be more geoducks in the world!
reading_mnemonic: The only person that would even hear the geoduck's request was Gandhi (がん). Gandhi closed his eyes, sat down, and spread the geoduck's request to the rest of the world.

meaning_mnemonic: The rice you feed to a big geoduck can be of any type, kind, or category. It doesn't matter what kind of rice it is, the big geoduck will eat it.
reading_mnemonic: While eating every type and kind of rice from every category, the big geoduck has become even bigger. Its body is ruined (るい). It's painfully obese. This geoduck has eaten itself to ruin.

meaning_mnemonic: The fly radical and the fly kanji are exactly the same! Awesome!
reading_mnemonic: When you fly, you generate a lot of heat (ひ) because you’re moving so fast through the atmosphere. Normally this heat would be a nuisance, but you’re a superhero so it doesn’t bother you. This is actually the reason you’re able to fly – you’re a superhero and super resistant to heat.

meaning_mnemonic: The radical neck and the kanji neck are exactly the same!
reading_mnemonic: The only thing you do with your neck is use it to swallow lots of cool beans (くび). Mm mm. Feel those cool, cool beans sliding down your neck. You don't really taste them, but you know they're there.

meaning_mnemonic: The horse radical and the horse kanji are exactly the same! Huzzah!
reading_mnemonic: You are looking at a horse. It's looking at you. You try making horse noises at it, to get a reaction. Instead of reacting with a normal horse noise, it just makes sheep noises: "Baaa," (ば) it says. "Baaaaa."

meaning_mnemonic: When the mouth of a bird opens, you're most likely to hear a chirp. This is how birds communicate. They open their mouths and let out a series of chirps. Chirp chirp chirp!
reading_mnemonic: The best way to experience the chirp-chirping of birds is to offer them nachos (な). Birds love nachos so much, it's a guaranteed way to make them chirp with delight.

meaning_mnemonic: The leader of your clan wants to live close to the ground so he demands you get low. Low, low, with your belly to the ground. That way you're always below him, since he's the leader.
reading_mnemonic: Low people like you can only eat low food like potatoes. But that's boring, so you low people learned to make tater (てい) tots. You roll them to each other and eat them without lifting your heads.

meaning_mnemonic: The leader's mouth has grown old from saying so many things. This is what makes them different from everyone else, they speak truly like an individual.
reading_mnemonic: As an individual, they must teach all the 子s (こ) their way. Their individual way.

meaning_mnemonic: This cage with treasure in it is actually a map of the district the treasure is in.
reading_mnemonic: There is one district you're interested in, and that's the cookie (く) district.

meaning_mnemonic: Next to the cross we combine our power power power so that we have cooperation. And with our powers combined, we become stronger than we ever could have been apart, lifting the cross above our heads!
reading_mnemonic: Nowhere is the power of cooperation more apparent than in きょうと. When invaders are attacking, when the townspeople want to rebel, when there is a kitty up a tree, the people combine their power from all reaches of Japan and cross into きょうと to put a stop to the madness through cooperation.

meaning_mnemonic: Use your mouth to take a measurement of this group. Just stretch your mouth out and around every single person. Get 'em all in there.
reading_mnemonic: This group is so big it takes you till dawn (だん) to get your measurement: they weigh a ton (とん) too!

meaning_mnemonic: A grain woman is a woman who talks about grain with other women on a committee. Together they're known as the Committee of Grain Women. What does this committee discuss, you wonder.
reading_mnemonic: Well, they formed this committee because eagles (い) have been eating all the grain. The women meet as a committee and try to come up with ways to stop these pesky eagles from eating all the grain and leaving none for the humans.

meaning_mnemonic: A bird sits upon a mountain. If you look at the radicals, the bird is quite large and the mountain quite small. Think of this in the mnemonic as well. The reason the mountain is small is because you can only see the top of it, sticking out of the water. On it is the bird. This small mountain with the bird on it is an island.
reading_mnemonic: But this island doesn't only belong to the bird. In fact, the bird shouldn't be on this island, because it belongs to the Sheep Mama (しま), who is like Mother Nature but for sheep. The all-powerful Sheep Mama comes to kick the bird off the island, because this place is only for sheep! All hail the Sheep Mama.

meaning_mnemonic: Think about Japan. Japan is a country made up of islands. They're basically three drop drop drops in the large river that is the Pacific Ocean. These are Japan's states or provinces.
reading_mnemonic: Each state has its own shoe (しゅう) to represent it. The bottom of each shoe is the shape of the state, so when you step it leaves a state-shaped imprint in the ground.

meaning_mnemonic: A canopy attaching your entire country is the government. They loom over you all and try to keep you all organized and together under their control.
reading_mnemonic: Try to get out from under this government canopy and you'll be labeled a fool (ふ). Unless... you can fool them!

meaning_mnemonic: You can make your fingers branch out. It's your special skill, a very advanced technique. Your fingers branch out into smaller fingers and you can hold things really well. You can type super-duper fast. And you can win any tickle fight. These are skills you have thanks to your branching fingers.
reading_mnemonic: Unfortunately, these skills are too much for the normal skill-less people to handle, so they pull out the guillotine (ぎ). I guess they're going to chop off your skillful fingers because they're kinda scary.

meaning_mnemonic: It's important to focus oneself in winter so that one can emerge renewed! You can't really go outside in winter without getting cold or sick, so spend winter focusing on YOU.
reading_mnemonic: Winter ends and, renewed, you come out ready to start a new hobby: kayaking (かい)! Nothing says renewal like a brand new kayak and sense of purpose in life.

meaning_mnemonic: Someone's taking tree measurements… Why are they taking measurements of trees? Because they're planning to cut them down to make their village.
reading_mnemonic: They take all the wood back to where they're building their village, and once they construct the village center they paint a mural (むら) on the side of it. The mural is of the forest where they got the trees from, to honor the village's origins.

meaning_mnemonic: If a tree is growing out of a top hat you need to inspect it to find out why and how this happened. You should probably investigate the area too. I mean, how could a tree grow out of a top hat anyway? Seems suspicious.
reading_mnemonic: As you inspect the tree, you pick up a saw(さ) and start cutting it. You need to investigate how the tree and the top hat are connected, and a saw is the only way to do it properly.

meaning_mnemonic: The compare radical and the compare kanji are exactly the same! Huzzah!
reading_mnemonic: Compare the heat (ひ) today with the heat yesterday. Is it hotter today? It's up to you to compare.

meaning_mnemonic: Direct a tsunami into a canine's mouth to decrease the amount of water that strikes the surrounding area.
reading_mnemonic: After you and your canine decrease the tsunami's power, Genji (げん) comes out to thank you. That tsunami was on track to wash away Genji's house, which would have forced him to majorly decrease his frivolous playboy activities.

meaning_mnemonic: Some of your grain has just been taken by a guard. This is the tax you pay for living in this town. Back in the day, grain was used like currency, so it makes sense that guards went around collecting grain tax.
reading_mnemonic: You have to pay this tax, because if you don't the guard will cut you down with his special German saber, a zeiber (ぜい). "Don't you hear vat I zei? Pay ze tax or I vill zlei you vis my zeiber!" he shouts.

meaning_mnemonic: If someone sticks bamboo in your eye twenty times, the first thing your brain does is calculate how painful it is. Your brain's pain calculation will determine how you calculate your next move.
reading_mnemonic: Next you want to calculate how much punishment your bamboo attacker deserves, so you call on Santa-san (さん). Santa-san is always calculating how many pieces of coal the naughty children deserve, so he's perfect for this calculation job.

meaning_mnemonic: Taking out your thread, you sew together the public's hearts to make them whole again.
reading_mnemonic: Once their hearts are whole, the public's soul (そう) becomes one!

meaning_mnemonic: You can use a long piece of thread during white water rafting as a safety line. Sure it's thin, but if someone goes overboard even a line of thread is better than nothing. Throw them a line and drag them back aboard!
reading_mnemonic: The person who threw you that line of thread is actually a centaur (せん). How kind of him. After you are safe you hop on the centaur's back and ride around to get the wind to dry you off.

meaning_mnemonic: That outfit on your skin is there to cover you up. In polite society, it's expected that you cover your skin with some kind of outfit — even if you have to wear something that causes you to incur damage, like circulation-cutting skinny jeans or a shirt with a really scratchy tag.
reading_mnemonic: Another reason to cover yourself is to retain heat (ひ). Actually, retaining heat and staying warm is probably the reason people started covering themselves up in the first place.

meaning_mnemonic: If you say a new weapon idea out loud, then it will be established immediately.
reading_mnemonic: Weapons have to be established in sets (せつ). So you have to make another one that goes with it. Make them cohesive please.

meaning_mnemonic: The Viking opens his mouth, and below it, a shellfish sits. Grab that shellfish and throw it into his mouth to win a prize!
reading_mnemonic: The prize you're working so hard to win is lunch with the Shougun (しょう). This is a pretty huge prize, considering all you're doing is knocking something over.

meaning_mnemonic: You run into someone's forehead with your car. The big forehead you hit is Kim Jong Un's. You know that now you're going to have the whole North Korean army coming after you.
reading_mnemonic: The army is after you. Each army soldier has a gun (ぐん) and they want to use these guns of theirs to shoot you dead! You killed their leader with a car and now they’re gonna get you back with a gun!

meaning_mnemonic: You blast your music loud so it causes a landslide, revealing the perfect soil for farming! Musically moved dirt is perfect for agriculture.
reading_mnemonic: The first person to come up with this farming method was Nostradamus (のう), the famous seer and prophecy man. He predicted humans of the future would use special "yell cubes" to "move that good earth."

meaning_mnemonic: While riding your scooter, you take your sword and cut out an area on the ground. You carefully cut all the sides as you go. This area's all yours now!
reading_mnemonic: As you look down at your area with its sword-carved sides, you suddenly realize there is a hen (へん) pecking at the ground in there. "Um, excuse me, hen, I believe I said this is MY area?!" You try to kick it out, but it hops over your leg.

meaning_mnemonic: If there is a building in the direction you want to go it will prevent you from going any further. Like, come on kid, you think you can just walk right through a building? Don't make me laugh!
reading_mnemonic: The building is preventing you from going the right direction, so you pull a bowling (ぼう) ball out of your bag, aim, and bowl the building over. The building, and all the ones around it, go tumbling down. But now the rubble is preventing you from going further.
